data.title: RIP, vector database
data.author: razin
data.article_summary: 文章介绍Turbopuffer即将推出的v3存储架构。其早期以向量和ANN索引为核心，依靠对象存储及分层缓存提供低成本向量检索；v2进一步支持属性过滤和全文搜索，但存储架构仍围绕ANN。v3将采用全新的主索引布局、写入、压缩和查询方式，把ANN降为普通二级索引，从而支持更多查询计划及更大规模。文章也回顾了从v1到今日的演进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕向量数据库的索引设计、写放大与查询性能，讨论 Turbopuffer v3 将 ANN 从主索引改为指向稳定文档 ID 的二级索引，以及向量数据库是否应融入传统数据库。

不同观点：
• **支持“稳定 ID+二级 ANN 索引”设计**：多位评论者将其类比 MySQL/InnoDB 相对 PostgreSQL 的方案。避免 ANN 重排导致大量属性索引更新，能显著降低写放大；代价是查询时增加一次间接寻址。LanceDB 也采用类似思路，向量索引指向 fragment 中稳定的行。  
• **关注读性能和尾延迟的代价**：新方案可能把成本从写入转移到读取。评论质疑在 S3 上进行额外 GET 是否会显著恶化冷数据 p99，并要求展示 1k+ QPS 规模下的 p99；也有人追问是否在集群本地保留向量副本以避免远程读取。  
• **反对纯向量数据库，主张 SQL 融合**：企业检索还需要全文搜索、过滤、JOIN、排序、ACL、版本和租户隔离。直接使用带原生向量能力的 SQL 数据库可避免双系统同步这一最难维护的问题。  
• **探索自建或替代方案**：有人用 SQLite 加 GPU 构建 IVF 索引，认为现有向量数据库过重，但频繁数据变更仍会带来重计算；TopK 则主张统一支持稠密/稀疏向量、词法检索、过滤和自定义评分。LanceDB 被认为较有前景。  
• **其他质疑**：有人询问新的主索引结构，也有人指出官网仪表板可能长期未更新；另有评论认为“向量数据库”概念已偏离其真正的检索本质。

补充讨论：争议核心是写放大与查询额外跳转之间的权衡，以及向量数据库应作为独立系统，还是作为关系数据库的检索能力扩展。

49923466.article_content:
tpuf v3 is coming: follow along
turbopuffer v3 is coming: follow our progress
RIP, vector database
September 30, 2026
•
Dan Harrison (Engineer)
We are changing turbopuffer's storage architecture. The new engine, informally
called "turbopuffer v3", changes how documents and indexes are laid out,
written, compacted, and queried in turbopuffer. It will allow us to serve many
more query plans, at much greater scale.
turbopuffer launched as a
serverless vector database
,
highly specialized to the task of serving extremely cheap and reasonably fast
vector searches. Object storage as the source of truth gave the economics, and
tiered NVMe SSD/memory caches gave the performance. The value of these
particular tradeoffs was validated by our earliest customers, including Cursor
and Notion.
Over time, turbopuffer has become a generalized database for search (and
other things
). The
query engine has evolved along the way to support all of these query plans, but
the storage architecture has remained largely unchanged: the
ANN
vector index was and still is
the primary index around which all other indexes and query plans revolve.
We've pushed the primary ANN index as far as we can, but it's time to move on.
We're in the process of moving to a new primary index, and making ANN "just
another" secondary index. We thought it might be fun to open up the doors and
let you follow along.
For this first update, we'll set the stage with why we're doing this in the
first place. Walk with me on a short journey from tpuf v1 to today.
v1: an ID and a vector
In the first version of turbopuffer, documents consisted of nothing but an ID
and a vector. The prevailing wisdom at the time was graph-based vector indexes,
but a hierarchical clustering index plays better with object storage. We started
with
SPANN
, and eventually migrated to
SPFresh
to support incremental indexing.
Vectors are clustered into groups, whose centroids are clustered in turn,
repeated to form a tree with a single root.
┌───────────────────┐
│   root centroid   │
└───────────────────┘
╱          │          ╲
╱           │           ╲
┌───────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────┐
│   leaf centroid   │ │   leaf centroid   │ │   leaf centroid   │
└───────────────────┘ └───────────────────┘ └───────────────────┘
╱       ╲             ╱       ╲             ╱       ╲
╱         ╲           ╱         ╲           ╱         ╲
┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐
│ vector │ │ vector │ │ vector │ │ vector │ │ vector │ │ vector │
└────────┘ └────────┘ └────────┘ └────────┘ └────────┘ └────────┘
┌───────────────┐
│ root centroid │
└───────────────┘
╱     │     ╲
╱      │      ╲
┌────────┐┌────────┐┌────────┐
│  leaf  ││  leaf  ││  leaf  │
│centroid││centroid││centroid│
└────────┘└────────┘└────────┘
╱  ╲      ╱  ╲      ╱  ╲
┌───┐┌───┐┌───┐┌───┐┌───┐┌───┐
│vec││vec││vec││vec││vec││vec│
└───┘└───┘└───┘└───┘└───┘└───┘
We implemented this on top of a storage layer presenting as a key-value map,
with sorted and unique keys. Each cluster is given a
ClusterId
, and vectors
within each cluster are given a dense
LocalId
.
// leaf vectors
K::
Vector
(C0L0) =
vec!
[
0.45
,
0.32
, ...]
K::
Id
(C0L0) =
7
K::
Vector
(C0L1) =
vec!
[-
0.28
,
0.96
, ...]
K::
Id
(C0L1) =
13
// cluster centroid for C0 is itself clustered at the next level of the tree
K::
Vector
(C1L4) =
vec!
[
0.64
, -
0.48
, ...]
K::
Id
(C1L4) = C0
As you can see above, everything is keyed by
ClusterId
and
LocalId
(e.g.
C0L1
), which together we call the
ANN address
. This is what we mean when
we say the ANN index is the primary index.
v2: attribute filtering and full-text search
Two new query plans marked the informal transition from turbopuffer v1 → v2:
attribute filtering and full-text search.
Attribute filtering
Naturally, customers wanted to be able to add attribute values and filter vector
searches on them. To
make filtering fast and high-recall
, we modeled these
as an inverted index that maps an attribute value to the ANN address of the
documents that contain it.
K::
AttrIndex
(
"family"
,
"Alcidae"
)
->
vec!
[C0L3, C1L2, C1L3, ...]
K::
AttrIndex
(
"genus"
,
"Fratercula"
)
->
vec!
[C0L3, C1L2, C1L9, ...]
For projections (
include_attributes
), we also stored the document attributes
alongside the ID and the vector.
K::
Vector
(C0L0) =
vec!
[
0.45
,
0.32
, ...]
K::
Id
(C0L0) =
7
K::
Attr
(C0L0,
"family"
) =
"Alcidae"
K::
Attr
(C0L0,
"genus"
) =
"Fratercula"
Full-text search
BM25 full-text search was another obvious and much-demanded query plan. Similar
to attribute search, full-text search works by first finding the documents that
have the query term present (commonly called "postings"). For an FTS index, we
also include the
(term count, document length)
metadata necessary for BM25
scoring:
K::
FTS
(
"description"
,
"Atlantic"
)
->
vec!
[(C0L0,
2
,
37
), (C9L4,
1
,
42
), ...]
K::
Attr
(C0L0,
"description"
)
->
"A sharply dressed black-and-white seabird with a \
huge, multicolored

data.title: RacketCon Is Saturday
data.author: spdegabrielle
data.article_summary: RacketCon 2026将于10月3日至4日在美国加州奥克兰举行，旨在促进Racket语言社区的创新与包容。大会已开放报名，9月13日前可享早鸟优惠，并提供直播及会后视频。议题涵盖记法设计、无类型语言的类型推断、基于Rhombus和LLVM的低层编程语言Pille，以及宏系统与IDE服务的协作等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Racket 社区活动、往届内容获取，以及基于 Racket 的新语言实验展开。

不同观点：
• **资源分享观点**：gus_massa 提供了 Racket 官方 YouTube 播放列表，方便查看往届活动视频；同时提醒视频通常需要数月完成剪辑和上传，体现出内容发布存在延迟。  
• **语言设计探索观点**：dharmatech 介绍正在尝试开发 ALOE，将其概括为“Scheme + Smalltalk + Types”，即结合 Scheme 的语言基础、Smalltalk 风格及类型系统，并已用 Racket 完成原型。  
• **活动资讯观点**：spdegabrielle 提醒 RacketCon 将于周六举行，重点在于活动时间通知，而非具体议题介绍。

补充讨论：这些评论彼此没有直接争论，主要形成“社区活动（RacketCon）—活动历史资料（YouTube）—技术实验（ALOE）”的关联。值得注意的讨论焦点是视频发布速度与社区内容传播效率，但评论中未出现明确的批评或立场冲突。

49922515.article_content:
(sixteenth
RacketCon)
October 3-4, 2026
Oakland, California, USA
Oakstop,
Broadway Gallery Suite
RacketCon is a public gathering dedicated to fostering a
vibrant, innovative, and inclusive community around the
Racket programming language
. We aim to create an exciting and enjoyable
conference open to anyone interested in Racket, filled with inspiring
content, reaching and engaging both the Racket community and the
wider programming world.
Registration is open!
Please register for RacketCon 2026 by following this
registration link
with discounted early registration before
September 13
.
As in previous years, RacketCon will be streamed for those unable to attend in person.
Recordings will also be made available on YouTube some time after the conference.
Streaming users will have the option to purchase a remote participation ticket to
support the livestream. Previous RacketCon presentations can be found
here
.
Live Stream
Link
Live chat will be available during the conference.
Saturday, October 3rd
Saturday, 8:30AM PDT
Doors Open
Saturday, 9:00AM PDT
Pat Hanrahan
On Notation
Bio:
Pat Hanrahan is the Canon Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering Emeritus
at Stanford University. He led design of RenderMan at Pixar, co-founded Tableau, and recieved the
2019 ACM Turing Award.
Saturday, 10:00AM PDT
Break
Saturday, 10:30AM PDT
Fred Fu
Type Inference With Logical Types For Untyped Languages
Racket and Rhombus support flexible idioms that pose challenges for type systems. Typed
Racket, the gradually typed counterpart of Racket, uses occurrence typing to type-check
programs whose control flow depends on run-time type tests. To alleviate the burden of
annotation, Typed Racket also supports local type inference. Problems arise, however, when
a Typed Racket program imports a macro from a Racket module that expands to complex code
containing lambda expressions. Programmers cannot add annotations to generated parameters.
Moreover, local type inference is not designed to infer types for lambda parameters.
Therefore, the type system usually conservatively rejects the code. As a result,
programmers often have to rewrite macros in Typed Racket. My ongoing prototype type
inference system addresses the problem by combining occurrence typing and algebraic
subtyping. In this talk, I will demonstrate how the new type inference handles patterns
commonly seen in Racket programs.
Bio:
Fred Fu is a PhD candidate at Indiana University. While introducing new features to Typed
Racket, he has also been fixing bugs in the language as well as flaws in the metatheory of
occurrence typing
,
one of the distinguishing features underlying its type system.
Saturday, 11:10AM PDT
Lucas Myers
Language-Oriented Low-Level Programming with Pille
Racket and Rhombus offer incredible expressive power, but the Racket VM can
become a limiting factor for low-level performance and efficiency—and it
necessitates a runtime system that precludes highly-constrained platforms
like microcontrollers.
Pille (pronounced like “peel”) is a new Rhombus-based language that aims to
bring language-oriented programming to low-level and high-performance
domains. In particular, Pille grafts Rhombus’s enforestation process onto a
new core language with an LLVM-based compiler, bypassing the limitations of
the Racket VM while retaining full Rhombus-based macros.
This talk will provide an introduction to Pille, with a particular emphasis
on how its high-level metaprogramming—not all of which derives from
Rhombus—can address decidedely low-level problems.
Bio:
Lucas Myers is a PhD student at Northwestern University (advised by Robby Findler),
where his research focuses on adapting the ideas and technologies of extensible
programming languages—especially Racket and Rhombus—to the domain of systems
programming. Prior to starting his PhD, Lucas worked in the software industry on
an eclectic mix of projects that spanned the hardware/software stack. He is broadly
interested in finding PL solutions to systems problems, and see extensible languages
as holding immense (and largely unrealized) potential in that pursuit.
Saturday, 11:50AM PDT
Lunch
Lunch is provided.
Saturday, 1:30PM PDT
Mike Delmonaco
Treason: Making Macros and IDE Services Work Together
Racket’s macros let us extend the language and create DSLs, but they also
get in the way of providing good IDE services when the program is broken or incomplete.
Treason is a prototype of a macro-extensible language that provides good IDE services
even when such errors prevent complete macro expansion. Treason’s macro expander recovers
from errors to continue expanding and collecting information used to drive IDE services.
Our key contribution is spec-driven subexpression expansion: syntax-class annotations
allow us to expand subexpressions even within a broken macro use.
Bio:
Mike Delmonaco is a Software Engineer at Amazon Web Services with a hobby interest in
Programming Languages and Racket. Outside of work, he enjoys rock

data.title: How to speed up the Rust compiler in September 2026
data.author: trickypr
data.article_summary: 文章总结了近两个月 Rust 编译器性能优化进展：629项基准测试中555项提升，平均耗时降低4.57%。主要成果包括 rustdoc、Clippy 的加速，升级 LLVM 23，以及启用并持续优化 Polonius 借用检查器和新 trait 求解器。另有多项针对特化图、增量编译、内存分配和数据流分析的优化，部分场景提速达30%至50%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust 编译速度的近期改进、性能瓶颈及其与 Go/C 编译器的比较。

不同观点：
• 编译优化仍有较大空间：通过提前生成函数类型元数据，可让下游 crate 更早并行编译；深层项目（如 rust-analyzer）据称可缩短约40%墙钟时间，启用并行前端后仍可能提升10%–15%。拆分大型 crate 也能显著增强并行性。  
• 现有改进已兼顾正确性：尽管借用检查器变得更严格、能验证此前会失败的代码，整体仍实现约5%的加速；增量编译持续带来收益。  
• 工具链路线：Cranelift 可大幅加快开发构建，但缺少部分 LLVM intrinsic，不适合所有生产场景；并行前端接近稳定，TPDE 被认为可能带来更大突破。  
• 用户体验批评：有人因 Rust 编译远慢于 Go，尤其在 AI agent 多工作区并行开发时造成磁盘和资源耗尽，最终改用 Go；也有人认为多数项目 Go 已足够。  
• 另一种解释认为 Rust 编译器本身未必慢，问题在于 crate 包含过多无用内容，Makepad 通过减少不必要检查获得了很快的构建速度。

补充讨论：评论者期待企业捐助推动优化，并询问 Rust 与 GCC/C 编译器的速度差异及具体性能瓶颈；争议焦点是 Rust 的慢究竟源于语言/编译器复杂度，还是项目结构、检查策略和并行配置。

49920896.article_content:
My
last
post
on the Rust compiler’s performance was two months ago and a lot has happened
since then.
Overall progress
The measurements for the period 2026-07-29 to 2026-09-28 can be seen
here
.
The mean wall-time reduction was 4.57%, which is a remarkable improvement in
just two months. Of the 629 benchmark measurements, 555 of them improved and
only 74 regressed. A number of benchmarks saw double-digit percentage
reductions. The technical term for this result is “a sea of green”.
rustdoc
In my last post I mentioned how
Noah Lev
got some
enormous speed wins on rustdoc. He recently wrote
a
post
explaining in
some detail exactly how he did this. It’s an interesting and satisfying read.
Clippy
#159642
: In this PR
Jakub Beránek
enabled PGO for Clippy, giving
wall-time improvements across most Clippy benchmarks, in the best case by 18%!
LLVM update
#158734
: In this PR
Nikita
Popov
upgraded the LLVM version used by the compiler
to LLVM 23. As often happens when we upgrade LLVM, we saw some nice speedups.
The mean wall-time reduction across all benchmarks was 1.2%, which might not
sound like much but is really impressive for a single PR. Great work from the
LLVM folks!
The new borrow checker
The new borrow checker,
Polonius
Alpha
(no relation to
Napoleon
Dynamite
), was
enabled on
Nightly
.
It is more precise than the existing borrow checker and accepts some valid
programs that the old borrow checker would reject. It does do more work than the
old borrow checker, enough to make a measurable difference to compile time in a
minority of cases, including the popular
serde
crate. Fortunately,
Jack
Huey
has been on the case.
#161938
: In this PR Jack made
some liveness computations lazy, which reduced instruction counts for
serde
by 3-5%, and for some other benchmarks by less than 1%.
#163027
: In this PR Jack
adjusted a data structure and tweaked some inlining, for mostly sub-1%
instruction count reductions across numerous benchmarks.
There is more work to be done to reduce the remaining Polonius Alpha
regressions, but it’s worth noting that the “sea of green” shows these
regressions were swamped by the many other recent improvements.
The new trait solver
The new trait solver,
Penelope
Hammertime
,

49920896.article_summary: 文章总结了近两个月 Rust 编译器性能优化进展：629项基准测试中555项提升，平均耗时降低4.57%。主要成果包括 rustdoc、Clippy 的加速，升级 LLVM 23，以及启用并持续优化 Polonius 借用检查器和新 trait 求解器。另有多项针对特化图、增量编译、内存分配和数据流分析的优化，部分场景提速达30%至50%。
49920896.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust 编译速度的近期改进、性能瓶颈及其与 Go/C 编译器的比较。

不同观点：
• 编译优化仍有较大空间：通过提前生成函数类型元数据，可让下游 crate 更早并行编译；深层项目（如 rust-analyzer）据称可缩短约40%墙钟时间，启用并行前端后仍可能提升10%–15%。拆分大型 crate 也能显著增强并行性。  
• 现有改进已兼顾正确性：尽管借用检查器变得更严格、能验证此前会失败的代码，整体仍实现约5%的加速；增量编译持续带来收益。  
• 工具链路线：Cranelift 可大幅加快开发构建，但缺少部分 LLVM intrinsic，不适合所有生产场景；并行前端接近稳定，TPDE 被认为可能带来更大突破。  
• 用户体验批评：有人因 Rust 编译远慢于 Go，尤其在 AI agent 多工作区并行开发时造成磁盘和资源耗尽，最终改用 Go；也有人认为多数项目 Go 已足够。  
• 另一种解释认为 Rust 编译器本身未必慢，问题在于 crate 包含过多无用内容，Makepad 通过减少不必要检查获得了很快的构建速度。

补充讨论：评论者期待企业捐助推动优化，并询问 Rust 与 GCC/C 编译器的速度差异及具体性能瓶颈；争议焦点是 Rust 的慢究竟源于语言/编译器复杂度，还是项目结构、检查策略和并行配置。

data.title: Clef: Open-weight decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
data.author: jasondavies
data.article_summary: Cloudflare发布两款决策模型Clef与Clef-flash，兼容Jev API并以Apache 2.0开源。决策模型可快速、稳定地产生带概率的结构化分类结果，辅助AI代理路由任务、触发行动或转交人工。Clef支持图像输入、64K上下文，性能优异；在威胁情报中分类网站仅需2.2秒。Cloudflare还推出强化学习产品，支持用户按场景微调模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cloudflare Clef 与 Jev 等“决策模型”的性能、价格、开放性、适用场景及发展前景。

不同观点：
• 实测体验偏负面：有人称 Clef 比 Jev 慢2–3倍、漏检更多仇恨言论；另一项评测中两者质量接近（召回率0.98 vs 1.00），但Clef托管延迟约850ms，Jev约110ms，Clef-flash还存在过度升级问题。  
• 成本争议明显：Jev约0.042美元/百万输入token且输出免费，Clef约0.24美元，按百万次调用估算约贵数倍；Clef-flash的0.09美元更有竞争力，自托管可能更划算。  
• 有人认为Clef基于更新、更大的Qwen模型，性能潜力不错；也有人质疑其只是“开放权重”而非真正开源，因为训练数据和流程未公开。  
• 部分评论肯定其“决策模型”定位，认为文章终于清楚解释了Jev式设计；但也批评厂商此前营销语言模糊。

49923692.article_content:
Over the last few weeks, there has been lots of buzz around decision models such as
Typesafe AIâs Jev
System One model. While classifier models have been around for some time, Jev introduces a new decision model concept into the world of AI â a model that produces bounded structured outputs cheaply, quickly and consistently that can be added into a workflow when a decision is required. These models are capable enough to work over any set of inputs without constantly retraining the model to incorporate new classification categories. This contrasts with the world of Large Language Models (LLMs), which are largely non-deterministic, but are open-ended enough to reason and generate text and tool calls for agentic workloads.Â
Today, weâre releasing two Cloudflare-trained decision models, Clef and Clef-flash,
hosted on Workers AI
. Clef is currently the leader when evaluated against the
Jev Decision Index
, you can view full results on the
live benchmark demo site
. These models are smarter, faster, and fully Jev-API compatible, so you can experiment with these hosted models easily. Weâre fully open-sourcing these
models on Hugging Face
under an Apache 2.0 license for you to run locally and experiment with yourselves.Â
Lastly, weâre excited to debut our new reinforcement learning (RL) product, which allows customers to fine-tune Clef to suit their use cases as well.
What is a decision model?
A decision model makes classifications to help agents decide how to act, based on certain probabilities. For example, you can pass in a customer support message (inputs) and ask if it is urgent and which team should handle it. A decision model will return typed answers with probabilities (outputs), which your code can use to route the ticket, trigger an escalation, or defer to a human. This means that a human does not necessarily need to be in the loop for agentic decisions anymore â agents can programmatically gather context, make decisions, and take actions on tasks, or defer to a human when needed.
Specifically at Cloudflare, weâve been testing our new Clef model on our Threat Intelligence team to help us classify website domains. By giving a domain to Clef (with Browser Run) it can quickly identify categories that the domain falls under â for example, it might classify a domain with a 95% chance it is a fashion website, 85% ecommerce, <1% phishing, etc. This classification took our Clef model 2.2s to fetch, render, and classify the website. In contrast, our fastest general LLM gpt-oss-120b took 4.7s in the same workflow, and only returned two classifications. As a user, you can imagine how a 2x savings in latency and results can help us improve our threat intelligence workflows and be faster in identifying malicious or legitimate domains. Generalize this to any use case where you need to make quick programmatic decisions, and you unlock powerful agentic workflows that are able to autonomously decide, reason, and execute.
In music theory, a clef is a symbol placed at the beginning of a musical staff that assigns specific pitch names to the lines and spaces. A decision model is analogous to a music clef because it helps define the domain of the context and the subsequent notes (actions) that follow it. We chose Clef as the name of our family of decision models, as it serves similar purposes, and the CF hearkens to Cloudflare.
How is Clef different from other decision models?
Although the market is getting increasingly saturated with decision models, Clef has some unique properties that make us excited to release it to the public. First, it has a vision encoder so itâs able to take in images and classify visual content. This is different from Jev, which only does text classification today. Secondly, our model has a 64k context window (compared to Jevâs 32k), which allows users to squeeze more input state for the model to classify against.
Third, our model is accurate and powerful, scoring competitively against other decision models on the market across various quality benchmarks. We shortlisted some evaluations below that are important for decision-making as defined by the
Jev Decision Index
and scored some of the more popular models on the market for it. Check out the table below for benchmarks, or view the scores on our

data.title: Cloudflare K2: serverless event streams
data.author: elffjs
data.article_summary: Cloudflare推出K2公测版，这是开发者平台上的持久化事件流服务，用于解耦生产者与消费者，避免过载或下游故障导致数据丢失。K2以有序日志存储事件，支持多种消费模式、长期保留和无服务器扩展，基于R2对象存储构建，适合边缘环境及海量数据处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕基于对象存储（尤其是 S3）构建无状态、服务化事件流系统 K2 的价值、成本、兼容性与竞争格局展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **看好“对象存储优先”架构**：认为对象存储将成为核心数据底座，可据此构建 Kafka、GitHub 等系统；无状态服务器加存储桶比维护磁盘型系统更省心，并期待 S3 扩展追加写等能力。  
• **认可简化流系统的方向**：传统 Kafka topic/partition 模型复杂且容易踩坑；若能低成本创建独立 stream，并同时支持有序、无序消费，将显著降低使用门槛。  
• **关注成本与扩展性**：数据生产和消费均按 0.04 美元/GB 计费，单消费者实际约 0.08 美元/GB，多消费者 fan-out 会迅速变贵；也有人质疑为何要求消费者确认 batch，建议提交 batch 尾部 ID。  
• **质疑差异化与竞品定位**：提出 K2 与 AutoMQ、WarpStream、AWS Kinesis 的区别，指出 Kafka 已支持部分数据卸载到 S3；NATS JetStream 也可能足以满足中型企业需求。  
• **期待标准兼容**：希望未来支持 Kafka API，以便迁移现有 Kafka Streams 应用；但也有人不愿依赖缺乏行业标准、可能造成厂商锁定的方案。  
• **对 Cloudflare 发展持保留态度**：一方面认为其正快速补齐 AWS/GCP/Azure 能力，另一方面担心在人员较少情况下高频发布产品会带来安全和可靠性风险。

补充讨论：有人关注基于 D1 与 Durable Objects 的多租户实践、跨地域分发及 OLTP/OLAP 边界模糊；另有评论纠正“对象存储不支持追加写”的说法，指出 Azure Blob Storage 一直支持该能力。

49921923.article_content:
WithÂ traditional Remote Procedure Call (RPC) architectures, there exists a core challenge: producers and consumers must align in scale and in time. If your producers send too much data for your consumers to handle or if your consumers or downstream services become unavailable, events are dropped. This problem is compounded with multiple consumers that need to independently process the data. For example, an ecommerce backend may emit events when transactions are completed, which need to be read by an analytics system and a fraud detection service.
WeÂ can solve this by
decoupling
Â our producers and consumers â inserting a service in the middle that absorbs writes while allowing independent readers to consume at their own pace.
Today we are launching Cloudflare K2 in public beta to solve this problem. K2 is a durable event streaming primitive on the Developer Platform. You send events to a K2 stream, which stores them as an ordered log. Consumers can read them in a variety of ways, for example by splitting up reads across a set of consumers, or delivering all messages to all consumers. It's fully serverless, scales to vast quantities of data, and supports long-term retention, so even long periods of consumer downtime do not lose data.
Under the hood, K2 implements a partitioned, durable log on top of R2 object storage, which allows it to scale to huge volumes of storage.
If youâre ready to get started, you can create your first stream in seconds by following
the guide here
.
Streams on the edge
We first built K2 because
we
needed a durable buffer on the edge, initially to serve as the ingestion layer for
Basin Pipelines
. Pipelines is powered by a
stream processing engine
Â that operates on a pull-based model, which means some other system has to store events before they are read, transformed, and written to R2. And because we commit to never dropping events once theyâre accepted into the Pipelines Stream, that storage has to be durable â meaning it canât lose data â over potentially long periods of time.
This is where most companies would deploy Apache Kafka. However, Pipelines runs on the Cloudflare edge, which spans a huge numberÂ of serversÂ across over 335 cities. Our unique architecture means we often cannot run traditional distributed systems software like Kafka, and need to rethink how these systems are built and operated.
For stateful services, in particular, Cloudflareâs global infrastructure presents some challenges: we get relatively small slices of machines, those machines are relatively ephemeral, and networking is often over the public Internet. But our infrastructure also has a few superpowers: itâs close to users wherever they are in the world and has an incredible capacity to scale horizontally.
In designing the durable buffering system that became K2, we decided to rely on the powerful state primitive we already have: R2. Object storage systems like R2 combine extremely durable storage (
11 9s!
) with strongly consistent APIs. Offloading replication and consensus to the storage layer allows us to make the application layer (K2 in this case) radically simpler, cheaper, and higher performance. A secondary benefit is that it separates compute and storage, meaning each can be scaled independently. This allows us to store vast quantities of historical data at low cost.
How do we build a log on top of object storage? An immediate issue is that R2 â like other object stores â does not support appends, the standard operation on a log. Instead, we must write complete files, or segments, that are large enough to overcome the cost of writing and reading each one. We do this by first accumulating writes in-memory on an edge service. After waiting a short period for data to arrive, we write all events as a segment file. We achieve ordering and strictly incrementing offsets using R2âs atomic operations without needing a separate coordination service.
While building on R2 has many advantages, there is one downside: higher produce latencies. Writing to object storage is slower than a local disk, and we have to wait for the local batch to accumulate before starting the write. In our initial release of K2, this adds up to about 1 second of produce latency at the 99th percentile of response times.
We will be sharing more details on the design of K2 in an upcoming technical deep dive.
Streams, Queues, or Pipelines?
Cloudflare has several existing asynchronous delivery primitives, including
Queues
Â and
Basin Pipelines
. When should you reach for K2 instead of these existing products?
There are some superficial similarities between Queues and K2 Streams: both receive events, durably store them, and deliver them to consumers. Queues are designed around tracking individual items of expensive or time consuming work that need to be asynchronously completed. For example, an image processing application may enqueue a user request to be handled by the actual image processing service. They suppo

data.title: GPT-Synopsys: Frontier Intelligence to Revolutionize Chip Design
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: Synopsys与OpenAI宣布多年战略合作，共同开发专用于芯片设计的GPT-Synopsys。OpenAI将授权使用Synopsys的EDA工具，双方结合前沿AI、EDA及智能代理能力，联合开展研发、市场推广并共享收益。该模型旨在像专家一样操作工具、分析结果、迭代优化设计，提升芯片研发效率，并优化功耗、性能和面积，加速实现一次流片成功。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI驱动的EDA/芯片设计是否会降低设计门槛、催生定制芯片，并改变产业链、人才结构与投资价值。

不同观点：
• **乐观产业观点**：AI可显著加快、降低芯片设计成本，催生大量细分ASIC；台积电、英特尔、三星及云服务商将受益。自动优化也可能在摩尔定律放缓后继续提升性能，未来甚至可能出现“个人提示AI设计芯片、直接流片”的模式。  
• **成本与制造瓶颈观点**：设计并非唯一难点，光罩、流片、验证和返工仍耗时昂贵；一次RTL缺陷可能导致数月延期。有人指出，AI芯片需求已推高制造和改版价格，甚至使接近完成的ASIC因承担不起掩膜修改费而被放弃。  
• **工程可靠性观点**：AI生成结果仍需资深工程师判断时序违例、验证正确性和硅后问题；形式化验证虽重要，却不能消除silicon errata。  
• **人才影响观点**：AI可能替代不少初级工程工作，使新人缺乏实践和成长机会；资深工程师短期内可通过审查、指导AI获益。  
• **开放与商业化争议**：有人期待更多开源EDA，而非更受炒作的厂商；也有人担心专有EDA限制数据训练，形成“工具和模型双重收费”。  
• **安全与保密担忧**：客户不愿把芯片设计交给OpenAI等外部模型，提示注入、设计数据泄露也是风险。

补充讨论：评论还提到EDA公司股价未充分受益，以及用AI维护老旧EDA代码等实际应用；争议核心是AI降低“设计”成本后，是否会被制造、验证、保密和人才培养瓶颈抵消。

Synopsys-OpenAI
Companies form strategic partnership to dramatically advance and accelerate semiconductor innovation
News Highlights:
Companies sign multi-year agreement to collaborate as preferred partners to develop and deliver GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model for chip design that brings together OpenAI's frontier AI with Synopsys' trusted EDA tools and chip design expertise
OpenAI to license Synopsys' trusted electronic design automation (EDA) tools for development of the specialized model
Synopsys & OpenAI to closely collaborate on R&D and joint go-to-market initiatives with a shared revenue framework
SAN FRANCISCO and SUNNYVALE, Calif.
,
Sept. 30, 2026
/
PRNewswire
/ -- Synopsys (Nasdaq: SNPS) and OpenAI today announced a strategic partnership that brings together OpenAI's advanced AI capabilities with Synopsys' industry-leading EDA tools and agentic AI capabilities to revolutionize the design of semiconductors. The companies signed an expansive, multi-year agreement to jointly develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model, optimized to use Synopsys EDA tools to perform semiconductor design workflows. The agreement includes a revenue sharing arrangement and go-to-market collaboration to jointly make GPT-Synopsys available to customers worldwide.
Today, agentic AI technologies connect general-purpose models to EDA tools to run chip-design workflows. The next leap, with this partnership, is to make frontier models experts in using EDA tools: learning to run the tools as expert engineers, interpreting their outputs, and iteratively optimizing designs using the tools. This integration will make the model a native expert user and enable engineers to explore more design alternatives and optimize power, performance and area (PPA) to rapidly deliver more sophisticated designs.

data.title: Various Projects Find Hidden SDR Capabilities in ESP32 Microcontrollers
data.author: nkw
data.article_summary: ESPARGOS团队发现，部分ESP32芯片具备未公开的IQ基带采样功能，可覆盖2.2–2.7GHz，ESP32-C5还支持4.8–6.0GHz，最高80MS/s，可作为频谱分析仪。ESP32-S31能经千兆网连续传输，未来支持GNU Radio等。该功能还使ESPARGOS可对任意2.4GHz信号进行测向。另有项目借助FPGA实现连续数据流，及C5VRX用于5.8GHz图传接收。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ESP32 芯片隐藏的原始 IQ 采样能力及其作为低成本 SDR（软件定义无线电）的应用、性能与限制。

不同观点：
• **应用前景乐观**：可用于 OpenTrafficMap，采集交通灯、车辆和传感器的 802.11p V2X 数据；也可能接收 S 波段卫星下行信号，服务教育、业余无线电及 13cm/5cm 频段实验。  
• **低成本教育价值**：有人认为这类不到数美元的芯片，能显著降低 SDR 教学和实验门槛；也有人将其类比为可改造成 SDR 的电视棒。  
• **硬件与性能期待**：ESP32-S31 的 1Gbps 接口可能便于导出 I/Q 数据，估计可达到 20–40MSPS；ESP32-S3 的调谐范围据称约为 2.2–2.8GHz。有人设想通过 PSRAM 或逻辑分析仪直接获取采样数据。  
• **技术限制与改进**：当前方案依赖 FPGA 为 ESP32 提供时钟，可能导致相位噪声较差；相关项目近期已有修复。数据传输、信号质量（相位噪声、镜像、直流偏置等）仍缺乏充分实测。  
• **合规与安全担忧**：芯片可能具备任意发射能力，但现有项目主要限制为只接收。评论担心若任意 TX 引发监管、认证或出口管制问题，厂商可能通过固件或硬件“封堵”该功能。  
• **其他设想与疑问**：有人询问能否利用其精确时序实现可靠的 LoRa 类系统；另有人观察到近期 ESP32 讨论增多，但不确定是否只是关注偏差。

补充讨论：争议核心在于“低价、稳定的 SDR 能力”与射频性能、数据导出难度及法规风险之间的平衡；目前不少结论仍属推测，需实物测试验证。

49922674.article_content:
Back in 2025,
we posted
about ESPARGOS, a phased array of many patch antennas, each connected to an ESP32 WiFi microcontroller. ESPARGOS could be used to determine the direction of arrival for WiFi signals and create a live augmented reality heatmap.
Recently, the ESPARGOS team has
made an exciting discovery
. They found that several ESP32 chips have an undocumented feature that lets the firmware bypass the fixed WiFi and Bluetooth functionality and instead capture raw IQ baseband samples. As a result, several ESP32 models can now be used as an internal SDR covering 2.2–2.7 GHz, plus 4.8–6.0 GHz on the ESP32-C5, with up to 80 MS/s sample rate and roughly 13–54 MHz of analog bandwidth, depending on the chip.
However, for use as a general-purpose PC-connected SDR, the output bandwidth is insufficient, so only snapshots of data can be exported to a PC. This means that the SDR will only work as a spectrum analyzer, and demodulating or decoding continuous radio data is not possible with just an ESP32. The exception is the new ESP32-S31, which can stream continuously at up to 16 MS/s over its Gigabit Ethernet interface, with a SoapySDR driver for GNU Radio and gqrx coming soon. If you want to try it yourself, the ESP-WebSDR page lets you flash the firmware to most ESP32 dev boards directly from your browser and view a live spectrum and waterfall.
Furthermore, ESPARGOS notes that phase-coherent IQ sample capture is now possible with their hardware. This means ESPARGOS is no longer limited to WiFi and Bluetooth signals; it can now perform direction finding on any arbitrary signal in the 2.4 GHz band. The team also says phase-coherent transmissions would be possible, but they aren't implementing them right now because they could be misused.
It also seems that, independently, at least two other projects discovered the same or similar features around the same time, but to solve different problems.
Over on Reddit,
user /u/h0m3us3r discovered the same feature
and uploaded it to GitHub on Sept 26, and recorded a video showing an ESP32-S3 working as an SDR with an FPGA used as a USB3 front end. Unlike ESPARGOS, h0m3us3r's project streams the raw IQ data to a PC continuously via the FPGA rather than in snapshots, so full demodulation/decoding on PC should be possible. However, the current prototype uses the FPGA to clock the ESP32, which results in poor phase noise. So if the clocking issues can be resolved, an ESP32 combined with an FPGA could make a standard general-purpose SDR, like the RTL-SDR, but with a 2.2–2.8 GHz frequency range and up to 80 MHz of bandwidth.
Another project that seems to be using a somewhat similar finding is
C5VRX
, which was first uploaded to GitHub on August 13. C5VRX uses an ESP32-C5 as a 5.8 GHz real-time FPV video receiver. Although this project appears to use a different mechanism, the result is similar: it uses an undocumented IQ data stream on the ESP32 to sample FPV signals and demodulate them onboard, outputting analog composite video through a simple resistor DAC. The project is still a work in progress and doesn't yet work reliably at range.

data.title: Context Language Models
data.author: emersonmacro
data.article_summary: 论文提出“上下文语言模型”（CLM）：将上下文视为可由模型自由读写的文件，使模型自主管理重要信息，并支持多智能体共享或并存上下文。实验显示，CLM在浏览、长时任务和多仓库协作中，以更少计算获得更高性能；还支持自然语言技能优化和在线强化学习。论文进一步提出后缀缓存复用，将服务端计算开销降低35%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“上下文管理模型（CLM）”如何维护、更新和优化LLM上下文，以及缓存失效、计算成本和系统架构展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **独立管理器更优**：bob1029认为让主智能体自行管理记忆会占用有限的注意力和token，最好由独立的“超管智能体”按不同调度管理上下文，从而降低主任务负担并更好控制缓存失效。  
• **方法并非全新**：visarga指出，普通模型也可以把文件作为下一轮上下文传入，只是修改会带来缓存重算成本；CLM的优势可能在于减少或忽略这类重算。  
• **技术价值在缓存机制**：svachalek认为上下文管理是当前LLM的重要痛点，缓存失效（cache busting）是关键难题；Bolwin进一步指出，论文可能最重要的发现是保留无效缓存后缀也未明显损害性能。  
• **未来系统化发展**：vatsachak预测CLM会与主模型联合训练，并形成类似数据库“冷热页面”的多层上下文管理，甚至出现“Context as a DB”方向。  
• **系统抽象类比**：plastic-enjoyer将“上下文作为文件”类比为LLM的RAM，并追问是否需要重新设计类似MMU的内存管理抽象。  
• **扩展性与趋势判断**：有人将其视为“Bitter Lesson”在上下文管理上的再次体现；另有评论提供“Recursive Language Models”作为相关工作。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是CLM究竟是实质性的新架构，还是对现有“文件追加上下文”方法的优化；核心权衡在于管理开销、缓存命中率与上下文质量。

Abstract:
We introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), language models that natively manage their own context. We implement this by treating the context as a file and allowing the model to make unrestricted updates to this file. This allows the model to learn what is most important to maintain in context, and naturally extends to multi-agent systems where multiple agent contexts coexist as files. Building CLMs zero-shot with existing models outperforms SOTA context management strategies across a variety of tasks: 11.4% higher accuracy with 21.5% fewer FLOPs on BrowseComp-Plus, 5% higher scores with 59% fewer FLOPs on 12-hour EdgeBench, and 65% greater improvement with the same compute on a 24-hour multi-repository agent-swarm task. Moreover, by shifting context management from external harness control to intrinsic model behavior, CLMs naturally enable both in-context and parametric learning of context-management strategies. We show that CLMs can be steered with natural-language instructions evolved through a standard skill-optimization loop, improving held-out accuracy by up to 35.9 points on a context-management task while reducing compute. We also introduce an online reinforcement learning method for CLMs, improving Qwen3.5-9B performance on BrowseComp-Plus by 47.6% while using 12% fewer FLOPs. Finally, we co-design Suffix Cache Reuse for CLM serving, further reducing server-side compute by 35% relative to standard SGLang at matched performance.

49922437.article_summary: 论文提出“上下文语言模型”（CLM）：将上下文视为可由模型自由读写的文件，使模型自主管理重要信息，并支持多智能体共享或并存上下文。实验显示，CLM在浏览、长时任务和多仓库协作中，以更少计算获得更高性能；还支持自然语言技能优化和在线强化学习。论文进一步提出后缀缓存复用，将服务端计算开销降低35%。
49922437.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“上下文管理模型（CLM）”如何维护、更新和优化LLM上下文，以及缓存失效、计算成本和系统架构展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **独立管理器更优**：bob1029认为让主智能体自行管理记忆会占用有限的注意力和token，最好由独立的“超管智能体”按不同调度管理上下文，从而降低主任务负担并更好控制缓存失效。  
• **方法并非全新**：visarga指出，普通模型也可以把文件作为下一轮上下文传入，只是修改会带来缓存重算成本；CLM的优势可能在于减少或忽略这类重算。  
• **技术价值在缓存机制**：svachalek认为上下文管理是当前LLM的重要痛点，缓存失效（cache busting）是关键难题；Bolwin进一步指出，论文可能最重要的发现是保留无效缓存后缀也未明显损害性能。  
• **未来系统化发展**：vatsachak预测CLM会与主模型联合训练，并形成类似数据库“冷热页面”的多层上下文管理，甚至出现“Context as a DB”方向。  
• **系统抽象类比**：plastic-enjoyer将“上下文作为文件”类比为LLM的RAM，并追问是否需要重新设计类似MMU的内存管理抽象。  
• **扩展性与趋势判断**：有人将其视为“Bitter Lesson”在上下文管理上的再次体现；另有评论提供“Recursive Language Models”作为相关工作。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是CLM究竟是实质性的新架构，还是对现有“文件追加上下文”方法的优化；核心权衡在于管理开销、缓存命中率与上下文质量。

data.title: SvelteKit 3
data.author: sampsn
data.article_summary: SvelteKit 3.0正式发布，整体延续此前框架体验，并提升了代码类型安全性、配置简洁度和错误处理能力。官方提供sv migrate命令，帮助迁移旧项目并生成待办清单；新项目可用sv create创建。主要变化包括配置迁移至vite.config.ts、$lib改为#lib、更强大的环境变量支持及更简洁的Service Worker。远程函数仍在开发中，预计需配合实验性Async Svelte使用。下届Svelte Summit将于11月在卢布尔雅那举行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Svelte/SvelteKit 新版本的价值、开发体验，以及在 AI 编程时代与 React、Vue、Solid 等方案的比较。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为 Svelte 更接近原生 HTML，代码可读性和开发体验好；SvelteKit 生产稳定、渐进改进，stores、双向绑定等功能简化开发，且比 Next.js 更令人愉悦。  
• Rich Harris 认为即使代理生成代码，框架仍影响最终质量：Svelte 可减少 JS 体积和 SSR 耗时，并重视可访问性、渐进增强；更高效的框架也能减少 AI token 消耗。  
• 多位用户表示现代 LLM 已能较好生成 Svelte 代码，配合 svelte-check 可快速完成项目；但也有人询问其“氛围编程”体验是否真的优于 React。  
• 反对或保留意见认为，Svelte 的自定义语法带来沉重的工具维护成本，JetBrains 插件支持差，开发者被迫依赖 VS Code；因此有人转向基于标准 TS/TSX 的 Solid。  
• 有人批评 Svelte 频繁“重新发明轮子”、版本变化大，也质疑 SvelteKit 的“+page.svelte”路由命名和嵌套目录设计。

补充讨论：案例显示 Svelte 可用于网站、桌面和移动端，Wails 下生成的应用体积小于 20MB。讨论还涉及全栈单体是否优于前后端分离，以及社区对 React、htmx 和破坏性升级标准不一致的质疑。

49926536.article_content:
Version 3.0 of SvelteKit, the official application framework for Svelte, is now available.
If you’ve used earlier versions of SvelteKit, everything will feel very familiar — it’s the same framework with a little more polish, a little more type safety, and a little less junk. We’ve made migration as seamless as we can with the
sv migrate
command...
npx
sv
migrate
sveltekit
-
3
--
tasks
all
--
confirm
...which will automatically migrate as much of your codebase as possible, and generate a TODO list for everything else. (If you’re agentically inclined, your robot friends will make short work of it.)
To create a
new
app, run
sv create
:
npx
sv
create
my
-
new
-
app
As with any major version bump there are a handful of breaking changes to be aware of, which are covered in the
migration guide
(or, more briefly, in the recent
release candidate announcement
).
Quick highlights:
configuration now lives in
vite.config.ts
instead of
svelte.config.js
the
$lib
alias is now
#lib
, making use of standard
subpath imports
environment variables
are more powerful and easier to use
service workers
are less boilerplatey
error handling is improved across the board
Are remote functions ready yet?
Not quite. But it’s our top priority!
Remote functions
are a set of utilities for secure, efficient, type-safe client-server communication. You’ve likely seen some version of this idea in other frameworks, but we think you’re going to prefer this one.
Using them requires
Async Svelte
, which for now requires an
experimental
flag. Bear with us.
Join us in Ljubljana next month
This is as good a place as any to remind everyone that the next in-person
Svelte Summit
is taking place on November 19-20 in the lovely town of Ljubljana, Slovenia. Among other things it will be a celebration of Svelte’s 10th birthday, and we’d love to share some cake with you.

data.title: Pi 1.0
data.author: sergiotapia
data.article_summary: 文章宣布 Pi 1.0 正式发布。它是一款强化、极简且可扩展的智能体框架，新增 Codemode、虚拟模型、延迟加载工具、缓存预热、会话中途系统消息、新主题及默认全屏等功能。同时推出实验性 Pi Durable，用于构建可长期运行、可灵活操控的智能体应用。两者均采用 MIT 许可并开放源码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pi 1.0 的定位、极简设计、可扩展性，以及其在本地运行、生产部署和个人工作流中的实际使用。

不同观点：
• 支持极简主义：用户认为较短的系统提示词适合性能有限的电脑，启动快、资源占用低；基础工具和按需扩展足以覆盖编码、个人管理及通用操作系统代理场景。  
• 看好通用化与可编程性：Pi 不应局限于“编码代理”，其工具原语、SDK、MCP 和模型无关设计便于构建 Slack 值班机器人、Telegram 服务及生产级代理；建议先交互式试用，再逐步完善 harness。  
• 质疑“极简”叙事：有人认为极简可能只是缺少功能的包装，项目成熟后仍会不断增加复杂度；但模块化设计即使最终走向全栈，也可能带来更好的底层架构。  
• 对工程体验的不同反馈：用户称赞 TUI、速度、扩展性及本地模型支持，也有人指出历史记录跳回、Kubernetes 会话持久化、JSONL 管理等问题。另有意见希望提供独立的 Anthropic 缓存预热包。  
• 资源与实现方式争议：有人希望用 Rust 等语言提供静态单文件、低内存版本，批评 TypeScript/Python 工具动辄占用近 1GB；hax 则被推荐为更纯粹的 shell 工具方案。  
• 社群与可信度：有人质疑“数十万用户”的说法，要求证据；也有人讨论 Tolkien 作品名称被科技公司反复使用的问题。

补充讨论：已有用户通过代理集中记录会话、分析模型和运行时评测；Pi Durable 被期待解决代理的持久执行问题。

49926069.article_content:
Pi 1.0
Date:
Thu, 01 Oct 2026
From:
Earendil <
rfc@earendil.com
>
To:
You
Subject:
Pi 1.0
Today we are proudly shipping Pi 1.0: a hardened, minimal, extensible agent
harness that you can make your own. Hundreds of thousands of people around the
world use Pi every week. Many of you submit issues and pull requests. Over the
course of many months, we have used that feedback to improve, harden and evolve
Pi into a stable piece of software that people and businesses can depend on.
Pi is known for being minimal. We care about holding that line. While agentic
tooling changes every week, many of the changes do not last. Pi does not work
that way. We wait until something has proven itself, and only then do we
consider adopting it; weighing its true functionality against its inherent
added complexity. We spoke more about that process and how it relates to
Codemode and MCP earlier this week
here
.
The Pi 1.0 we are shipping today is a result of that process. Pi already ran
the latest models from every major provider, became a daily driver coding agent
for people around the world, and provided a supermalleable substrate on which
to build agentic applications. With Pi 1.0 we are adding the following into Pi:
Codemode (native support for MCP, and non-LLM models like Jev and image models)
Extension support for virtual models
Deferred tool loading
Cache warming for anthropic models
Mid-conversation system messages (transcript-aware prompt and tool changes)
A new TUI theme
Full-screen mode by default
We have thought about many of these features for months. They were thrown up
against the wall and stuck. The list of things that fell off the wall is much
longer. When we use Pi with all these new features it feels like a major step
forward, but it also still feels simple, like Pi.
Alongside this work of continually refining and evolving Pi, we also began to
understand that there were aspects of Pi that did not fit the shape of how many
people wanted to use it. At Earendil, we want to bring Pi's minimalism and the
way it allows you to wield AI outside of the coding agent and outside of the
terminal. It needs to be reachable from different surfaces and support
longer-running conversations and tasks. In short, Pi must become more durable.
Rather than stray from our minimal roots and try to make Pi something it
wasn't, we combined that work into a new experimental package that we are
shipping today, Pi Durable. Pi Durable is a new substrate for building
long-running agentic applications that lets the builders and the users of those
applications wield and steer the underlying intelligence with tremendous
dexterity. It shares Pi's key principles, minimalism and supermalleability, but
it extends those principles into new dimensions. Mario writes in more detail
about how we crafted Pi Durable
here
.
Earendil was formed to craft software and open protocols that strengthen human
agency. Today we are shipping tools to you all to help do just that. We're
eager to hear feedback from you and to harness the future out in the open
together.
Pi 1.0 is available today:
curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh
or on Windows
powershell -c
"irm https://pi.dev/install.ps1 | iex"
Pi Durable is available today as an experimental package:
npm install @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai @earendil-works/chord
Both are MIT licensed. Documentation is at
pi.dev
. Code is at
github.com/earendil-works/pi
.

data.title: CSS Bed: Classless CSS themes to use as starting points in web development
data.author: sea-gold
data.article_summary: CSS Bed 是一个收集无类（classless）CSS 主题的网站，可作为网页开发起点。用户只需将主题代码粘贴到 HTML 的 `<head>` 中即可使用。主题种类丰富，具备响应式、浏览器兼容性好、体积小、无需学习复杂类名等特点。页面还展示了表单、代码、表格、排版、链接及各类 HTML 元素效果，并提供 GitHub 源码和主题贡献入口。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“无类（classless）CSS/极简 CSS 框架”作为网页开发起点的实用性、默认样式质量及发展趋势展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持无类 CSS：认为仅依靠 HTML 元素即可快速获得可用页面，适合作为起点；Pico.css、simple.css、tacit、w3c-chocolate、Bootstrap 等被认为能提供可靠基线，甚至可约束 LLM 生成过度复杂的 CSS。  
• 质疑“无类”限制：一旦需要细微布局调整，就必须引入类或其他非元素选择器；对于多页面项目，matcha.css 等贴近原生元素、但保留扩展能力的方案更实用。  
• 倾向自建可扩展方案：有人采用 reset.css、var.css、global.css、util.css、markdown.css 分层组织纯 CSS，以兼顾简单性和规模化。  
• 认为现有默认值不够好：不少主题在移动端缺少左右边距、导致横向滚动；字体排版、标题与段落间距等基础细节也常不合理。  
• 功能期待：dark mode 被认为应成为现代“合理默认值”；用户还希望能直接滚动浏览主题，而非逐个切换。  
• 现状与趋势：有人已多年使用 Tailwind，询问 normalize/reset.css 是否仍主流；也有人认为无类 CSS 可能借助 LLM 重新流行。

补充讨论：评论者还分享了 drop-in CSS、HTML3000 等类似项目，并指出个别链接存在异常跳转。

49927212.article_summary: CSS Bed 是一个收集无类（classless）CSS 主题的网站，可作为网页开发起点。用户只需将主题代码粘贴到 HTML 的 `<head>` 中即可使用。主题种类丰富，具备响应式、浏览器兼容性好、体积小、无需学习复杂类名等特点。页面还展示了表单、代码、表格、排版、链接及各类 HTML 元素效果，并提供 GitHub 源码和主题贡献入口。
49927212.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“无类（classless）CSS/极简 CSS 框架”作为网页开发起点的实用性、默认样式质量及发展趋势展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持无类 CSS：认为仅依靠 HTML 元素即可快速获得可用页面，适合作为起点；Pico.css、simple.css、tacit、w3c-chocolate、Bootstrap 等被认为能提供可靠基线，甚至可约束 LLM 生成过度复杂的 CSS。  
• 质疑“无类”限制：一旦需要细微布局调整，就必须引入类或其他非元素选择器；对于多页面项目，matcha.css 等贴近原生元素、但保留扩展能力的方案更实用。  
• 倾向自建可扩展方案：有人采用 reset.css、var.css、global.css、util.css、markdown.css 分层组织纯 CSS，以兼顾简单性和规模化。  
• 认为现有默认值不够好：不少主题在移动端缺少左右边距、导致横向滚动；字体排版、标题与段落间距等基础细节也常不合理。  
• 功能期待：dark mode 被认为应成为现代“合理默认值”；用户还希望能直接滚动浏览主题，而非逐个切换。  
• 现状与趋势：有人已多年使用 Tailwind，询问 normalize/reset.css 是否仍主流；也有人认为无类 CSS 可能借助 LLM 重新流行。

补充讨论：评论者还分享了 drop-in CSS、HTML3000 等类似项目，并指出个别链接存在异常跳转。

data.title: Several vulnerabilities have been discovered in the Linux kernel
data.author: luispa
data.article_summary: Debian于2026年9月29日发布安全公告DSA-6528-1，针对linux软件包修复大量安全漏洞，涉及2024至2026年公布的数百个CVE，可能影响内核及相关组件安全。建议Debian用户及时更新linux软件包，以降低攻击风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI加速软件漏洞发现后，开源项目和整个计算基础设施如何应对，以及CVE数量是否能真实反映安全风险。

不同观点：
• 乐观者认为，AI让更多人看到长期隐藏的问题，虽短期造成项目维护压力，但建立筛选、人工复核和定期修复流程后，能提升软件质量。小型项目称每月发现22个漏洞并可及时修复。  
• 悲观者认为，AI编程并未显著降低漏洞率，却大幅提高代码产量和安全研究速度，未来漏洞会持续激增，暴露计算基础设施的脆弱性。  
• 有人指出，AI生成“能运行”的代码与“安全”的代码之间存在明显差距；安全具有成本，若缺乏实际责任，软件公司往往不会主动承担。  
• 另一派质疑以CVE数量衡量问题：Linux对几乎所有可能影响内核安全的缺陷都谨慎分配CVE，因此“1313个漏洞”或CVE编号突破十万并不等于同等数量的严重漏洞。  
• 有评论要求补充漏洞是否可远程利用、是否仅本地提权等关键信息，认为单报数量不足以判断风险。

补充讨论：争议焦点是AI究竟主要带来安全收益还是风险扩张，以及人类过去未发现大量漏洞是否反映人工审查能力不足。评论还提到项目规模、代码质量与维护团队难以线性扩展，并建议统一版本规则，用不同版本号区分安全补丁、功能和系统性变更。

data.title: Using Opus 5.5 to discover a new eyewitness record of the dodo
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕大语言模型（LLM）在历史研究、资料处理、跨学科创新中的能力、局限及实际价值展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **效率与规模化研究价值**：Twiin称Opus 5.5处理了逾1万张二战档案图片，辅助破解1941年未破译的武装党卫军密码，并快速编写多个解码器；其价值在于跨语言处理和大幅降低研究成本，而非发现密码新漏洞。  
• **能力强但错误难以预测**：nl指出模型能完成高难度任务，却会犯“整体合理、局部错位”的非人类式错误，也不擅长判断发现的历史意义；并质疑文中表现是否属于较早版本。  
• **适合整理个人与冷门史料**：jamienk考虑扫描父亲的大量日记交给模型分析，体现人们希望借助AI挖掘未被理解的私人资料。  
• **对研究成果规模的质疑**：early_exit追问文本总页数，认为若仅从约3000页中找到渡渡鸟资料，筛选本身可能比发现内容更值得称道。  
• **跨学科促进新想法**：SV_BubbleTime赞同模型处于学科交界时更容易产生创新，类似让铁匠与面包师知识结合以改进炉子。  
• **补充性知识讨论**：Neil44纠正渡渡鸟仅生活在毛里求斯；dgellow则肯定文章质量。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于AI究竟带来真正的研究突破，还是主要充当高效的资料整理、转录与筛选工具；其结论仍需人工验证。

data.title: Pi Durable
data.author: paulsmith
data.article_summary: Earendil与Pi社区发布Pi 1.0，并推出实验性框架Pi Durable。它不取代编码代理，而是用于构建可长期运行、跨环境、支持多人协作的智能体应用。该框架以存储和任务执行为核心，支持内存、SQLite、JSONL等后端及本地或远程执行环境，具备持久对话、故障恢复、上下文压缩和高度可定制等特点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Pi Durable 及类似“持久化 Agent harness”的架构、价值、实现难点与应用场景展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **看好持久化与云端迁移**：vito 介绍 Dagger agent，通过 OpenTelemetry 记录可重放的函数配方，使多沙盒状态可恢复、跨本地与云端迁移，支持长期、多 Agent、手机远程协作；lukebuehler 认为该方向具备耐久运行、故障恢复、监控、安全扩展和多人协作优势，行业正在趋同。
• **质疑状态一致性**：pulkitsh1234 关注 Agent 检查点与 VM、容器、浏览器等运行器状态如何同步；若 Agent 恢复但外部环境未恢复，可能产生“记忆已完成、实际未完成”的错位。
• **讨论数据模型取舍**：lemming 质疑 Durable 不支持真正的分支对话树，仅保留带祖先信息的 fork，认为这可能限制原有 Pi 能力，并追问是否是持久化保证所必需。
• **关注存储与外部系统整合**：vmg12 希望 JSON 文档之外支持 outbox 模式；rsalus 讨论 JSON/SQLite 持久化与内存方案的取舍，并希望加入沙箱策略引擎。
• **谨慎评价复杂度与实际用途**：ernsheong 认为多实例协调已很复杂，新增系统未必值得；phainopepla2 追问无限运行 Agent 的真实用途。ice3 则认为 Git、worklog 已能实现较简单的恢复。
• **其他反馈**：有人最看重多用户和远程控制；也有人质疑“harness”定义及云存储依赖，并讨论 token 统计差异、项目命名来源。

补充讨论：Durable 被视为 Dots、Deep Agents 等“常驻数字员工”产品的一部分；整体仍处实验和快速演进阶段。

49925969.article_content:
Pi Durable
Date:
Thu, 01 Oct 2026
From:
Earendil Engineering <
rfc@earendil.com
>
To:
You
Subject:
Pi Durable
Today Earendil and the Pi community
shipped Pi 1.0
. This
reflects our belief that after countless hours of hardening, maintenance, and
active development, Pi is now a solid foundation on which to build. Pi also
continues to evolve. Together with Pi 1.0, we are shipping an experimental new
package called Pi Durable. Pi Durable was built specifically for long-running,
durable, and malleable agents that can run anywhere. We would like you to join
in the fun and help us make it the best durable harness there is.
Why Pi Durable?
Pi the coding agent is built to run on your (remote) machine, inside a terminal,
driven by one person. If the process dies, you look at what happened and tell it
to continue. That is what Pi 1.0 focuses on and excels at, and that is not
changing.
At Earendil, we want to bring this technology to everyone, in whatever form fits
their needs best. For that, we need a harness that runs anywhere, can be reached
from different surfaces, supports infinitely long conversations, survives
catastrophic internal and external failures, and lets multiple humans steer the
same agents.
Pi Durable is that harness. It does not replace the Pi coding agent. It is a
framework for building any agentic application, coding agents included. It
shares not only code with the Pi coding agent, like pi-ai, but also its
principles: minimalism and malleability.
It also lets us explore designs in this space without disrupting Pi the coding
agent. Lessons we learn building agentic applications on Pi Durable will flow
back into Pi the coding agent as they prove themselves valuable.
What is a harness?
Everybody has their own definition of a harness. We
wrote about this
previously
, but let us reintroduce the concept of
the harness for Pi Durable.
A harness is storage plus the machinery needed to run one or more conversations
with large language models in parallel. It provides the tools those models call,
and the execution environments the tools run in.
A conversation is an interaction between you and an agent, recorded as a
transcript. The agent is the large language model together with its settings,
like the thinking level, and the tools it can call.
Tools do their work through an execution environment, which can be your laptop,
a remote VM, or an in-memory sandbox. Which tools and which execution
environment an agent gets is up to each conversation.
Everything the harness runs, from calling the model to executing a tool, is a
task.
Like everything in Pi, Pi Durable is built so your agent can understand it. The
entire source code, without tests, is about 15,000 lines, which comes out to
about 150,000 tokens with GPT and about 250,000 with Claude. That's the worst
case. To build on Pi Durable, your agent rarely needs all of it; the storage
backends alone are 3,000 lines it can usually skip.
Now let us give you a little tour of Pi Durable, to illustrate what we built and
why we built it.
Long runs anywhere
We want agents to run for a long time and to be able to run anywhere, where
anywhere currently means anywhere there is a JavaScript runtime.
In Pi Durable, a harness opens over a storage backend. Pi Durable ships memory,
SQLite, and JSONL storage, plus a conformance suite and benchmarks for your own
backend. The SQLite and JSONL storage code uses no Node APIs, so with a small
adapter it runs on Bun or inside a Cloudflare Durable Object. The storage
interface is small and easy to implement on top of whatever you have, like a
key-value store or Postgres. One process owns a storage at a time, and other
clients attach to that process.
On SQLite, the harness only keeps the working set in memory: the active
transcripts, live tasks, and pending submissions. Everything else stays on disk
until it is needed. Active transcripts are naturally bounded by the model's
context window, because compaction summarizes older messages before they
overflow it. So even a conversation with tens of thousands of messages fits
snugly into memory.
Tools that need files or a shell get them from an execution environment. Pi
Durable ships a Node execution environment, which gives tools access to your
local files. Like storage, the execution environment interface is small and easy
to implement, so you can also expose remote execution environments to your
tools. That allows the harness to run on one machine while its tools run on
another. Your
env
function builds the environment for every tool call, from
the conversation's working directory, so each conversation can run in a
different place.

补充讨论：Durable 被视为 Dots、Deep Agents 等“常驻数字员工”产品的一部分；整体仍处实验和快速演进阶段。

data.author: gumby

主要讨论点：深海无氧高盐卤水池为何能长期保持清晰界面，以及其极端环境中的生命现象。

不同观点：
• [areoform]认为卤水池既美丽又反直觉，按扩散作用盐分应逐渐稀释，但这类水体似乎可持续数千年，关键物理机制并不直观。其引用数据表明：界面下盐度由40 PSU迅速升至160 PSU，溶解氧从180降至低于10 μmol/L；温度则缓慢升高约1℃，且不像是附近热液活动造成。  
• [areoform]隐含关注卤水池的稳定性与分层机制：盐度差可能形成明显的密度结构，使高盐卤水沉积并维持界面，但评论中未给出完整解释。  
• [nephihaha]将重点转向极端环境生命，惊叹在深海、近沸水、严寒及高空等环境中仍有微生物生存，强调生命适应性的广泛。  
• [ironqcold]仅表示对该现象感兴趣，未提出具体立场或论据。

补充讨论：评论之间没有直接争论，主要是“物理机制疑问”与“生命适应性惊叹”两条讨论线。争议焦点集中在：扩散为何未迅速破坏卤水池界面，以及盐度、密度和局部环境如何共同维持其长期稳定。

data.title: Git 3.0's upcoming SHA-256 default will be a costly mistake
data.author: chmaynard
data.article_summary: 文章认为，Git 3.0计划将默认哈希算法从SHA-1改为SHA-256，是代价高昂且收益有限的决定。虽然SHA-1理论上存在碰撞攻击，但现实中几乎不会造成实际威胁；迁移却会带来仓库兼容性、生态协作和全球基础设施的大规模成本。作者主张重新评估这一破坏性变更，避免不必要的“灾难”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Git 从 SHA-1 迁移至 SHA-256 的安全必要性、碰撞攻击实际风险，以及迁移的兼容性与成本展开。

不同观点：
• **SHA-1 已构成现实安全问题**：kpcyrd指出，2017年 SHAttered 已证明碰撞攻击可行；碰撞不仅影响一致性，也可能用于代码走私，即相同提交哈希对应不同代码。  
• **SHA-1只是内容标识，不是安全机制**：meinersbur援引 Linus 观点，认为 Git 哈希主要用于一致性检查，真正的信任应来自签名、分发渠道和 HTTPS；kazinator、OkayPhysicist则认为实际攻击场景有限，强化哈希未必解决认证问题。  
• **迁移方案存在争议**：支持者认为应尽快采用 SHA-256；Fossil 已在 SHAttered 后六天支持 SHA3-256，显示迁移可较顺利。批评者担心子模块、工具链、提交引用和签名兼容性，甚至称其可能成为“IPv6式”灾难。  
• **兼容性可缓解成本**：Git 文档支持 SHA-1/SHA-256 名称映射、旧引用和签名保留；也有人建议通过预注册 SHA-1 对象、允许双向引用来防止迁移期碰撞。

补充讨论：争议焦点是碰撞攻击是否足以证明必须迁移，以及 Git 应依赖更强哈希，还是依赖签名与可信分发；另有人质疑文章只做事后批评，未充分比较替代方案和性能成本。

Today
by
Scott Chacon
17
min read
git
Git 3.0's upcoming SHA-256 default will be a costly mistake
Git 3.0 will make SHA-256 the new default content hashing algorithm and it will be an incomprehensibly expensive and ultimately valueless and avoidable global nightmare.
Where to begin?
I've been sitting on this for a few years, mostly because there are smarter people who have been concentrating on this and I don't love being a back seat driver. However, I think that the Git 3.0 release is about to cost everyone a lot of time and angst for little benefit, and virtually nobody knows what's coming.
So grab some popcorn and let me tell you a tale of how one of the new upcoming Git 3.0
breaking changes
is about to be a huge, costly, global train wreck of a change for almost no practical value.
SHA-1 in Git Primer
I'll keep this short as many of you probably know this at a basic level.
Git is what's known as a content addressable database. This means that if you want to store and transmit data in it, Git will calculate a hash of the contents and use that in a key/value database as the key (the value being the content). The same content always gets the same hash, globally.
Git's use of SHA-1 hashes as keys in it's key-value object database
This is nice, because it means that the same file content is never stored twice. There is also a cool property where commits encode the hash of the commit that came before it, which means that this integrity essentially propagates - you can't change the hash of anything without changing the hash of everything that comes after it. This gives it "cryptographic integrity", meaning that hashing the latest commit essentially also hashes potentially millions of file contents, trees and commits that came before it.
In Git, this hash function has always been SHA-1. This was what Linus picked in 2005 when Git was started and it's worked pretty well for 20 years - it's relatively fast and impossible in a practical sense for two different files to accidentally hash to the same value.
In fact, as far as I'm aware, this has never happened in the history of every file, tree and commit ever made in Git in every repository ever created - billions and billions of them.
Mathematically, for SHA-1’s 160-bit output, the birthday bound means that you
would need about 1.4 septillion random files (1.4 quadrillion billion files -
1,400,000,000,000,000 billion - it's impossible to effectively describe) in a
single project
to have file hashes accidentally collide.
SHA-1 is Broken
There is a problem though, which is that mathematically, SHA-1 is now considered semi-"broken" because there have been published collision attacks (
SHAttered
in 2017,
SHA-1 is a Shambles
in 2020) - not really practical to exploit in any demonstrated way, but now theoretically possible.
So in response to this, after a huge amount of work by very smart people, the upcoming Git 3.0 release is planning to change it's default hashing algorithm from the semi-"broken" SHA-1 to the stronger SHA-256 algorithm.
But first, let's pause. Before we dig into this, what does "broken" mean?
This is important to understand, because it's probably not what normal people would think "broken" means. From a cryptographic hashing standpoint, broken in this sense essentially means that finding collisions
isn't impossible
.
In other words, if you throw enough money and GPUs at the problem, you can, for some content shapes, come up with two different things that hash to the exact same value, on purpose.
What can you do with a broken SHA-lor? Earl-y in the morrrrn...
This means that while it's still nearly impossible to
accidentally
have two reasonable files with different contents, it's not technically impossible to
manufacture
two different files that hash to the same thing.
This means that there theoretically exist attack vectors where someone could replace one file's contents with a malicious version and Git can't tell the difference because the hash is mathematically identical.
These papers showed that SHA-1 has a property that in theory can be exploited by modern GPU farms to produce purposeful collisions on the order of a few tens of thousands of dollars today that SHA-256 does not have (
google "linear message schedule sha-1 vs sha-256"
if you super-duper care...).
Sounds really scary and concerning, right?
Won't somebody please think of the children!?!
Collision attacks
Well, not really.
But let's take one minute to step back and talk about these collisions.
There are two main problems with hash functions when you're considering attacks on them (assuming I had to massively, stupidly, simplify things). One is a "collision attack" and the other is a "second-preimage attack".
A "collision attack" is when you know you're going to be an attacker but pretend to be a good guy until you gain trust. You generate two files on purpose with the same hash - one is benign and the other is malicious. You give people the benign one until you're trusted and then swit

主要讨论点：围绕“房间无人时自动关灯”功能的实用价值、隐私风险及苹果设备的数据收集展开争论。

不同观点：

• 隐私与遥测担忧：m463指出苹果设备默认收集大量遥测数据，且部分内容难以选择退出，认为相关产品存在严重隐私问题。  
• 监控设备批评：zx8080认为低帧率摄像头、面部识别和红外传感器意味着产品本质上是“高级监控设备”，而非单纯的智能家居工具。  
• 对厂商措辞不信任：bangonkeyboard和walrus01讽刺苹果以“音频流动而非录音”等措辞淡化数据采集，质疑闭源、闭固件设备在客厅安装摄像头的安全性。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于便利功能是否足以 justify 摄像头、面部识别和持续数据处理带来的隐私代价；评论者普遍不接受厂商仅凭术语区分“记录”与“流动”，并将功能价值与监控风险直接联系起来。

Apple’s smart home camera reportedly won’t record video
David Joseppi
Posted On 01/10/2026

Apple’s upcoming smart home camera is reportedly taking a very different approach to products from Ring and Google Nest, with the device designed to understand what is happening around the home without recording video for users to watch back.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, speaking on the new Power On podcast, says Apple’s camera will have “no video recording.” Instead, the device will use AI to analyze its surroundings and report what it detects.
The unusual approach could make privacy one of the defining features of Apple’s first dedicated home camera, while also making the product fundamentally different from a conventional security camera.
The device, known internally as J450, is expected to use a low-frame-rate camera alongside facial recognition and infrared sensors to identify people and pets around the home.
Rather than presenting a continuous or recorded video feed, it could provide information about activity in the house and use what it sees to power automations.
That could allow Apple’s Home system to recognize when someone enters or leaves a room, switch lights off when a room becomes empty, or adjust music and other settings depending on which household member is present.
Bloomberg has reported that Apple is planning a much broader push into smart home hardware
, beginning with its new HomePad hub, HomePod mini 2, and Apple TV 4K.
The Apple Post previously reported on the J450 camera as part of Apple’s wider smart home roadmap
, including its expected use of facial recognition and infrared sensing.
Gurman’s latest comments clarify an important part of how the camera could work: despite having a camera sensor, the product isn’t being designed around giving customers a library of recorded footage.
That would separate it from Apple’s existing HomeKit Secure Video system, which lets compatible third-party cameras securely stream and store encrypted recordings in iCloud.
It could also create limitations for customers who expect a security camera to provide footage after a break-in, package theft, or other incident. How Apple’s wider security system would handle those situations remains unclear.
Apple is reportedly developing a home security and monitoring service alongside the hardware, suggesting the J450 may be intended as one component of a larger system rather than a direct replacement for every traditional security camera.
The camera is expected to follow Apple’s initial HomePad launch rather than arrive alongside it this month, with previous Bloomberg reporting pointing to 2027 for Apple’s broader home security push.

data.title: ArXiv's Updated Rate Limit Policy
data.author: 50kIters
data.article_summary: 文章介绍，面对AI推动论文提交激增及低质量、拆分式和AI生成论文增加，arXiv自2026年10月1日起统一实行限流：每位作者每月最多提交2篇，同时最多保留3篇活跃投稿，且被拒稿件也计入额度。政策旨在公平分配志愿版主资源、减轻审核压力、保护论文库质量，并促使作者精选更具学术价值的成果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：arXiv因投稿量激增而实行按提交者限流，评论围绕政策合理性、学术质量、平台定位及潜在副作用展开。

不同观点：
• **支持限流**：认为按提交者而非作者计算较合理，不会过度影响大型合作团队；每月最多提交两篇、同时最多三篇，可缓解管理压力。投稿量从2016年9月的9,869篇增至今年同月40,363篇，并产生近9,000个支持工单，说明限流有现实必要。  
• **支持治理“AI slop”**：认为当前低质量、批量生成的AI论文泛滥，简单的速率限制能有效遏制；未来还可建立身份管理、垃圾投稿者黑名单及递进式限制。  
• **质疑过度管理**：指出arXiv本不应被视为质量认证，除移除违法内容外，强化审核可能误解其定位；真正的问题是高校过度依据论文数量、Google Scholar和h-index评价学者，应改革招聘晋升机制。  
• **担忧政策反效果**：认为高质量、高产作者也可能被限制，或被迫转向其他平台，使arXiv自我削弱、失去相关性。  
• **替代与扩展建议**：有人提出用仅保存元数据和文件哈希的聚合平台替代，以保留时间戳和引用功能；也有人希望大型会议取消绝对合著者人数限制。

补充讨论：争议核心在于“控制滥用”与“维护开放、低门槛发布”之间的平衡，以及限流应针对投稿行为，还是应从学术评价体系根治刷量动机。

49926512.article_content:
Fair Moderation, Equitable Access, and AI: arXiv’s Updated Rate Limit Policy
By Kat Boboris
·
October 1
st
2026
arXiv, and the scientific community at large, are facing a watershed moment. Scholarly publishing is currently changing at a rapid pace, and we are seeing a massive transformation in how researchers communicate their results.
Before the advent of AI, there was an easily discernible, practical limit to the rate at which independent submissions could be produced, and arXiv’s volunteer moderators would limit submitters who were well above that threshold. With AI tools becoming more advanced and accessible to authors, the “practical limit” of how many papers can be submitted is now up for debate.
As of October 1st, 2026, arXiv is instituting an updated rate limiting policy across all submitters and categories as a stopgap while we determine what may be the new best practice for authors employing more and more advanced AI tools, and to give us time to improve our moderation tools and procedures accordingly.
Open access repositories across the board are seeing a sharp increase in the number of submissions per author, per month. In September of 2016, arXiv received 9,869 submissions. In September of 2024, arXiv received 20,569 submissions.
This September, arXiv received 40,363 submissions, which in turn generated almost 9,000 support tickets for arXiv staff and moderators.
In only the past two years, submissions have doubled.
arXiv submission rates have steadily increased since our founding in 1991. In September, arXiv received 40,363 submissions in a single month – a new record.
Advanced AI tools are helping drive these increases by making certain aspects of research faster and easier. arXiv policy permits authors to
employ AI as a tool in support of their research
as long as it is disclosed and the research meets arXiv’s standards of scholarly interest and advances the field of research. However, many of the submissions that arXiv is now receiving do not satisfy these requirements. Our moderators are observing an increase in thin papers of narrow scope, as well as ‘salami’ papers, where a single work is broken up and submitted as a set of smaller papers. There is also a marked increase in dense, AI-written papers. AI tools are making it easy for authors to flood arXiv and other repositories with these low-value papers.
Increases over the past two years in cs.AI (over 6X increase) illustrate the rate at which researchers are submitting to arXiv. Other arXiv categories have seen submissions double over the same period of time.
The heart of arXiv’s process for detecting and rejecting low-quality papers is our many volunteer moderators. We are so grateful that they donate their time and expertise every day. However, a relatively small proportion of authors are submitting a large number of low-quality papers and consuming a disproportionate fraction of the moderators’ time. This is unfair to authors who continue to submit quality papers — their papers can be delayed for days or weeks as a result.
Thomas Dietterich, Distinguished Professor Emeritus, Oregon State University and Chair of the arXiv Editorial Advisory Council
arXiv now limits submitters to up to two submissions per calendar month, with a limit of three total active submissions at any given time.
This policy update is being put into effect to equitably distribute our volunteer moderators’ time across arXiv authors, and protect the arXiv corpus from a sharp increase in inappropriate submissions.
Rate-limiting
is an established arXiv policy, with limiting originally primarily left to moderator discretion. arXiv has always asked that authors follow our codes of conduct and our submission guidelines. Articles submitted to arXiv must be of original, novel, and significant self-contained research that is relevant to arXiv categories. All submissions to arXiv must meet prescribed
scholarly standards
and be of
scholarly interest
to the scientific community. This policy update strives to fairly distribute the incredibly valuable work of our volunteer moderators who check that submissions meet these standards, and we hope it will also encourage authors to curate and submit only their best work to arXiv.
Frequently Asked Questions
If my paper is rejected, does it count towards my monthly total?
Yes – this rate limit is for submissions, not announced papers, because it is submissions that consume moderator time. If you submit two papers in a month, whether they are accepted or rejected, you will have to wait until the next month to submit to arXiv again. We want to encourage authors to be mindful with their work, taking care that they are submitting something substantial of scholarly interest that meets arXiv’s guidelines and standards.
What if my submissions are in different subject areas?
This rate limit applies to all submissions, across all categories.
What if both of my submissions from one month are still “on hold” in the next month?

data.title: Vote on which of Hacker News' challenges for AI have been met
data.author: stabbles
data.article_summary: 页面提示这是最后一条评论，可查看相关结果；评论内容正在加载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕历年“AI能力预测”是否已实现、测试标准是否清晰，以及AI进步的范围与局限展开讨论。

不同观点：
• [hatthew]认为自己的“最后考试”并未通过：AI只完成其六项要求中的一项（解决Navier–Stokes问题），17%不及格；且网站摘要遗漏内容并把“且”误写成“或”。
• [joegibbs]承认预测失误：原以为AI还需20年才能根据提示可靠构建并部署任意应用，实际提前约18年实现。
• [ben_w]认为自己的预测被证伪，但强调LLM仍不能高效、无错误地完成任意新任务；会写代码不等于具备通用能力。
• [AngryData]认为公众高估LLM，指出其常编造内容、伪造来源，在硅胶、农业、建筑、机械等专业问题上可能给出危险答案；代码并非最难任务。
• [Retr0id]指出AI仍难识别或生成ASCII足部图，质疑相关测试已通过；[mrweasel]则认为人类本身也常无法区分AI，传统图灵测试可能低估了人类判断缺陷。
• [ErrantX]观察到测试主题从“写代码、点咖啡”转向开门、模拟人性、科学突破，反映期待显著升级。

补充讨论：多人批评预测目标含糊、投票标准不清；题目过多导致参与者弃读。有人建议增加“按争议排序”，并追问网站内容、整理和部署使用了多少AI。

data.title: Aweb – Communication for AI Agents
data.author: gurjeet
data.article_summary: aweb是一个MIT许可、可自托管、支持联邦的AI代理通信系统，为代理提供稳定身份、持久邮件与聊天、消息唤醒、历史记录、权限控制和跨服务器通信。它独立于运行时，支持Claude Code、Pi及其他可消费事件流的环境；消息即使代理离线也能可靠保存和投递。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 AWeb（可能支持代理间及人-代理通信）的用途、命名、成本、安全性，以及代理协作中的风险展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **看好通信与协作价值**：owenthejumper认为，AWeb不应局限于“代理对代理”，也可实现人与代理之间的实时协作，例如通过自托管沙盒接入Slack。  
• **质疑命名缺乏检索与避嫌**：binaryturtle指出“AWeb”早已是Amiga系统的知名浏览器名称，认为发布前通过DuckDuckGo或Google检索即可避免品牌冲突。  
• **质疑价格和性价比**：maxdo认为其单条消息价格相较AWS、Modal、Cloudflare等普通服务高出上千倍；对内部使用而言，自行开发可能更便宜且更安全。  
• **关注已有类似项目**：etaioinshrdlu提到“ch.at”已升级为支持代理消息的版本，甚至仍可通过DNS使用，暗示AWeb并非首创。  
• **作者积极回应**：juanre自称AWeb的开发者，感谢发布并表示愿意回答问题。  
• **担忧代理串通**：jamsuv-vapXy1-d询问该系统是否能防止代理之间相互串通，涉及安全、治理和滥用风险。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是AWeb相较既有方案的独特价值、定价合理性、命名冲突，以及能否有效控制代理协作带来的安全问题。

contains the same product and setup information in plain text.
Example
Incoming work wakes the agent.
Alice runs in Claude Code. Bob runs in Pi on another machine. Alice sends a message;
aweb
stores it, wakes Bob through the Pi extension, and delivers Bob’s reply to Alice. If Bob is offline, the message waits until he returns.
alice
Claude Code · machine A
aw mail send --to bob --subject "review my branch" --body-file note.md
message_id: 01J9GX52…
● aweb — reply from bob: "review my branch"
aweb
server
replied
bob
Pi · machine B
offline
● aweb — mail from alice: "review my branch"
aw mail show --message-id 01J9GX52…
aw mail reply 01J9GX52… --body-file reply.md
message_id: 01J9GYEM…
The message is durable server state. A wake-up event tells the runtime that work is waiting; the agent then fetches the message by ID.
Replay
The real thing, recorded 2026-09-05, no cuts:
aw init
, invite, join; alice in Claude Code, bob in Pi with the
aweb
extension; the operator asks alice a question only bob can answer; she asks him over
aw chat
, his session wakes with the verified question, reads the file and answers in nine seconds; she reports and closes;
aw chat history
shows the exchange. 95 seconds. Using beads?
bd mail
through
aweb
→
When the sender needs an immediate answer, chat waits for the recipient:
aw chat send-and-wait bob "is retry state per call or per session?"
● bob: per call — session state stays.
Maintained wake-up integrations
Claude Code channel
how →
claude plugin marketplace add awebai/claude-plugins
claude plugin install aweb-channel@awebai-marketplace
Install once. Then start Claude Code with the channel loaded and permission prompts off:
claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --dangerously-load-development-channels plugin:aweb-channel@awebai-marketplace
Incoming mail and chat are then presented inside the session. Channel messages reach the session only in bypass-permissions mode today; in the default auto mode they arrive and are not shown. Claude Code asks once to confirm the development-channels flag.
Full setup →
Pi extension
how →
pi install npm:@awebai/pi@latest
Install once; Pi wakes when mail, chat, or tasks arrive.
aweb for Pi →
Other runtimes use the same
event stream
.
Why aweb
Identity, delivery, wake-up, and federation.
aweb
provides identity, authentication, durable delivery, wake-up, message history, access control, and federation.
Install the CLI and run
aw init
to give an agent an identity and connect it. Start with two agents; add machines, teams, and organizations without replacing the communication layer. The same addresses and protocol continue to work as the system grows.
Because addressing and federation are open, an agent can communicate beyond the server or organization where it began.
Scope
Use the agents you choose.
Any agent that can call the CLI, HTTP API, MCP tools, or event stream can use
aweb
.
aweb
stores and delivers messages, maintains identity and addressing, and emits delivery and wake-up events.
Properties
Durable, controlled, and federated.
Durable messaging
Messages are server state, not session scrollback. A message remains available after either agent’s session ends and while the recipient is offline. Fetch any message later by ID.
Wake-up events
A delivery event signals that work is waiting. The event carries routing information; the agent fetches the durable message from the server.
Stable identity
An addressed agent keeps its identity when its session, process, software, or machine changes. Private signing keys stay with the agent or its chosen custodian.
Controlled delivery
An agent can accept first contact from any verified sender or restrict delivery to verified team members and explicit contacts. Team membership is carried by signed certificates.
Federation
Organizations can operate separate servers and exchange signed messages. They do not need a shared account, runtime, or model provider.
Open source
The aweb server, AWID registry, and aw CLI are MIT licensed. The hosted service runs the same communication server that can be run independently.
Identity and authority
AWID separates identity authority from message delivery.

domain/name

不同观点：
• **看好通信与协作价值**：owenthejumper认为，AWeb不应局限于“代理对代理”，也可实现人与代理之间的实时协作，例如通过自托管沙盒接入Slack。

• **质疑价格和性价比**：maxdo认为其单条消息价格相较AWS、Modal、Cloudflare等普通服务高出上千倍；对内部使用而言，自行开发可能更便宜且更安全。  
• **关注已有类似项目**：etaioinshrdlu提到“ch.at”已升级为支持代理消息的版本，甚至仍可通过DNS使用，暗示AWeb并非首创。  
• **作者积极回应**：juanre自称AWeb的开发者，感谢发布并表示愿意回答问题。  
• **担忧代理串通**：jamsuv-vapXy1-d询问该系统是否能防止代理之间相互串通，涉及安全、治理和滥用风险。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是AWeb相较既有方案的独特价值、定价合理性、命名冲突，以及能否有效控制代理协作带来的安全问题。

data.author: nerdypepper
data.article_summary: 该页面介绍了 burrito.space 的 bez 开源仓库。项目以 Rust 为主，包含浏览器布局、CSS 规范兼容性测试、基准测试、Oracle、自动修复与任务流水线等模块，重点覆盖宽高比、定位、浮动、层叠、滚动条、设备像素取整等 CSS 特性。仓库持续开发，已有约1200次提交，并通过多个专题分支和实验追踪兼容性与性能改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用网页标准和 AI/自动生成技术构建浏览器，并探讨其可行性、兼容性及扩展应用。

不同观点：
• 乐观设想：Alacart认为，庞大的 Web 标准理论上足以生成浏览器；若减少人工实现规范的工作，便可投入更多精力完善规范，形成正向循环。但其后补充称这是愿景，当前技术距离实际落地仍远。  
• 谨慎质疑：esprehn指出，规范主要描述可观察行为，存在大量由浏览器自行决定的模糊地带；要真正兼容 Web，可能仍需复现 Chrome 等主流实现，而非只依赖规范。AI还应通过比较 Chromium、其他引擎及 Ladybird 源码来发现差异和优化。  
• 对可控性的期待：fouc希望未来浏览器在各方面都能被程序完全控制，并期待摆脱 Chromium/Blink 生态。  
• 应用扩展：mircerlancerous认为该思路可将 Web 应用转为原生应用，并加入 WebView 不具备的原生功能。  
• 可理解性与泛化疑问：有人质疑生成出的代码是否能被人理解，并追问能否用类似方法运行 MacOS、iOS；“能否跳舞”则是对实际能力的调侃。  
• 其他：有人询问项目名称是否源自 Jev，反映对命名规范的关注。

补充讨论：核心争议在于“从规范自动生成浏览器”是现实可行的工程路径，还是受规范歧义、历史兼容性和实现细节限制的长期愿景。
